Operation

Read preprocessing

Remove adapters, primers, and low-quality sequence so downstream steps work from clean reads.

Inputs

  • Raw sequencing reads (FASTQ)

Outputs

  • Cleaned reads (FASTQ)
  • QC report

Preprocessing removes technical artifacts introduced during library preparation and sequencing, so that later steps measure differences between samples rather than differences between library preparations. Different artifacts need different treatments, so more than one method may apply to the same reads.

Choosing methods 2

These methods address different problems and can be combined. Apply each one whose conditions match your data.

  • Amplicon primer trimming

    Remove primer sequence from amplicon-based reads using a primer scheme.

    Use when

    • The library was made with tiled amplicons, such as ARTIC-style schemes.
    • You have the BED file for the exact primer scheme and version used.

    Skip this method when

    • The library is shotgun, so there are no primers to remove.
    • The primer scheme or its version is unknown, since trimming with the wrong scheme leaves primer sequence behind.

    Combine with

    • Quality and adapter trimming: Apply it first to remove adapters and low-quality bases, which primer trimming does not fully address.

    iVar trim

  • Quality and adapter trimming

    Trim adapter sequence and low-quality bases from reads.

    Use when

    • Reads may contain adapter sequence, which is true of almost all Illumina libraries.
    • Base quality drops toward read ends or varies between runs.
    • The library is shotgun (whole-genome or metagenomic) or amplicon-based. Apply it in both cases.

    Combine with

    • Amplicon primer trimming: Required in addition for amplicon libraries, because quality trimming does not remove primer sequence.

    fastp · Trimmomatic
